claims.text: The starting material consists of solid FeNiCrCoCu high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles.
The starting FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles possess inherent nanoscale compositional heterogeneity.
Surface compositional variations in FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles produce Cu-enriched regions.
Cu-enriched surface regions enhance local atomic mobility.
Enhanced mobility in Cu-enriched regions lowers the energy barrier for atomic diffusion.
Cu-enriched regions begin premelting earlier than compositionally homogeneous surface regions.
Distinct pre-annealing treatments can respectively homogenize the nanoparticle surface and accentuate Cu enrichment and surface heterogeneity.
The comparison will use identical in situ TEM heating conditions for the homogenized and heterogeneous groups.
Cu-enriched regions and associated defects mediate local variations in atomic mobility.
Cu enrichment lowers the local melting point.
Early atomic diffusion at Cu-enriched regions initiates premelting.
Cu-enriched regions act as nucleation sites that govern the onset and spatial progression of melting.
Particles treated to enhance surface heterogeneity will have a statistically lower onset temperature for surface diffusion and premelting than particles with homogenized surfaces.
Initial phase-transition locations will spatially correlate with regions of elevated Cu concentration and defect density.
Nanoparticles have high surface-to-volume ratios, making surface-controlled behavior plausible.
The proposed surface-heterogeneity mechanism dominates when surface phenomena control the phase transition.
In larger particles or bulk-diffusion-dominated samples, surface heterogeneity has a diminished effect on premelting onset.
Heating rate and other nanoscale phenomena may also affect the phase-transition behavior.

contradictions.description: The conditions state that only surface composition is varied, but defect density is also included as a mediator and predicted correlate. Because pre-annealing can change defects as well as composition, the proposed comparison does not clearly isolate surface composition alone.
